data.why: The viewer ships real bundled .mtj scene captures under viewer/samples/ (GPT-2 and Qwen2.5 runs), which is exactly the data format (.mtj) the viewer reads; there is nothing to author or upload since the page loads scenes via ?file= or the Open/drag-drop control.

goals: Scrub a single prompt's hidden-state trajectory layer by layer and see where its projected states pile up into basins
Compare multiple prompts (or models) on one shared density terrain to see where trajectories diverge and where they converge
Check which states' local neighborhoods survived the 2-D projection (amber marks on states that did not) before trusting any visual pattern
Read the density's bootstrap standard-error overlay to judge whether a terrain region rests on too few points to trust
Inspect the decode-axis view of a generation (gpt2-decode) to see how the trajectory evolves token by token during sampling, not just across layers
Compare two models' residual streams in shared readout space (models-qwen-gpt2) despite differing layer counts and hidden sizes

review.summary: The tree matches what the README says Mottled is for: scrub hidden-state trajectories over a density terrain, compare prompts and models, and check projection fidelity and density SE before trusting a basin. The evidence I sampled is accurate, but a few specific labels claim more than was seen, the SAE-feature and file-loading paths are missing, and the blast tasks still need a replay before filing.
